## Summary

かしん's answer to Mr_tamura: he too digs through papers, and the best backtests he's found use **VIX and VIX3M as primary signals to buy/sell volatility**. The four tables describe an escalating ladder (clearly reformatted from an academic study — exact paper not identified from the tweet; figures "net of 5bps transaction costs, backtest 2008-2025"):

1. **Passive** — short-vol base (VIXSHORT always on), size 20% VIX% notional.
2. **eVRP** — VIXSHORT only if expected variance risk premium > 0 and VIX < VIX3M (contango); Cash otherwise. Both long (VIXLONG if eVRP<0, VIX>VIX3M) and short variants appear in the table's ladder.
3. **eVRP + BoC** (backwardation-of-contango / term-structure gate refinement).
4. **eVRP + BoC + Sizing** — position 0.5×VIX% scaling. Signal 3:45pm, **MOC orders**, rebalance rules per strategy.

Calendar-year table highlights (net, 2008–2025): the full ladder returned **+86.9% in 2008** (S&P −36.8%) and **+42.3% in 2020** (crisis alpha from the long-vol branch), 2008–2025 nearly all-positive years (worst ≈ −1.6% to −1.9% in 2024/2025 for the strategy variants), while passive short-vol did −18.6%/−19.0%/−12.0% in 2008/2018/2020. Chart 1 equity curves: ladder compounds to ~$1,200-1,400 vs passive ~$100-400. Chart 4: an end-of-month SPY + vol-strategy mix weight study ("Improve Passive" label) — vol as an overlay improves risk-adjusted passive returns at moderate weights.

## Skepticism gates

Source paper unidentified — tables are a repackage, so the backtest methodology (vehicle! futures roll costs vs options vs ETFs, fill assumptions at MOC, exactly how eVRP is computed) is not verifiable from the tweet. Short-vol ladder tails: "VIXSHORT" strategies are one Feb-4-2018 ("Volmageddon") from catastrophic; 2018's −8.1% (eVRP+BoC row) is the tell. The +86.9% 2008 figure implies the long-vol branch captured the crash — long-vol implementations are notoriously cost-sensitive (spreads on VIX options/futures), and 5bps TCost is futures-tight optimism. Sizing at "0.5×VIX%" scales notional with vol level — path-dependent leverage needs careful margin modelling. AI-backtest context (the quoted tweet) is reminder that these circulate as folk-wisdom; treat as a research lead, not a strategy.
